newsitem.title: UK: Crotone developments key to zinc in short-term.
newsitem.headline: Crotone developments key to zinc in short-term.

text.p: Likely developments at the Crotone zinc smelter in Southern Italy probably hold the key to market movements in the short-term, London Metal Exchange (LME) trader Billiton Metals Ltd said.
There are plans to convert the 100,000 tonne a year smelter, currently owned by Enirisorse, to a nickel-copper refinery. Details are likely to be completed shortly.

"The consensus still appears to be that the sale to Osmium Holdings and subsequent conversion will go ahead. The timing of the subsequent conversion could prove to be critical," Billiton said in its latest weekly review.
Zinc has been the star performer on the LME this year, with prices up by some $300 and at the highest levels since September 1992.
Production cutbacks, fund interest, and expectations of falling stocks have all played a part in market strength.

Confirmation that Crotone was to close would boost the market further and although in the longer-term lost capacity will be well absorbed, there is still no denying that the outlook for this market is brighter than it has been for quite some time, Billiton said.
